dutchnova1-0001.text: Je moet nog even melk halen.
dutchnova1-0001.english: You still need to quickly get some milk.
dutchnova1-0001.scenario: You're making breakfast, but milk is missing. Explain the remaining errand.
dutchnova1-0001.explanation: Nog signals that getting milk remains unfinished; even presents it as a small task. The modal moet keeps halen as an infinitive at the end.

example.text: Ik blijf nog even in de supermarkt.
example.english: I'll stay at the supermarket a little longer.

dutchnova1-0001.text: Ik blijf nog even in de supermarkt.
dutchnova1-0001.english: I'll stay at the supermarket a little longer.
dutchnova1-0001.scenario: You're already shopping but want to look around a bit longer.
dutchnova1-0001.explanation: Because blijven is a continuing action, nog even means a short extension, not an uncompleted errand. The first person finite verb is blijf.

example.text: Je moet nog even melk halen.
example.english: You still need to quickly get some milk.

dutchnova1-0003.scenario: You already have one bag and need one more.
dutchnova1-0003.explanation: Nog een asks for an additional item; it does not imply a different type. In this yes/no question heb comes before je.

example.text: Heb je een ander zakje?
example.english: Do you have a different bag?

dutchnova1-0003.english: Do you have a different bag?
dutchnova1-0003.scenario: Your first bag is too small and you want a different bag.
dutchnova1-0003.explanation: Ander, without -e, modifies singular indefinite het zakje. This changes the goal from adding a bag to replacing it with another kind.

example.text: Heb je nog een zakje?
example.english: Do you have another bag?

dutchnova1-0019.text: Heb je vandaag al iets gegeten?
dutchnova1-0019.english: Have you eaten anything today yet?
dutchnova1-0019.scenario: Ask a friend who has been busy all day whether they have eaten yet.
dutchnova1-0019.explanation: Vandaag sets the time, al asks whether the event has happened by now, and gegeten is the participle of eten.

example.text: Ik heb vandaag nog niets gegeten.
example.english: I haven't eaten anything today yet.

dutchnova1-0019.text: Ik heb vandaag nog niets gegeten.
dutchnova1-0019.english: I haven't eaten anything today yet.
dutchnova1-0019.scenario: You have not had any food today; tell your friend.
dutchnova1-0019.explanation: Nog niets signals an expected but unrealised event. The negative word niets replaces iets in the statement; gegeten stays as the perfect participle.

example.text: Heb je vandaag al iets gegeten?
example.english: Have you eaten anything today yet?

dutchnova1-0022.text: Wacht nog even op de bus.
dutchnova1-0022.english: Wait for the bus a little longer.
dutchnova1-0022.scenario: The bus is late, but your friend wants to leave. Ask them to wait a bit longer.
dutchnova1-0022.explanation: Nog even extends the ongoing wait. Op is the fixed preposition after wachten; it should not be translated from English literally.

example.text: Ik moet nog even op de bus wachten.
example.english: I still need to wait for the bus for a moment.

dutchnova1-0022.text: Ik moet nog even op de bus wachten.
dutchnova1-0022.english: I still need to wait for the bus for a moment.
dutchnova1-0022.scenario: Your bus is due soon; explain the one remaining thing you're doing.
dutchnova1-0022.explanation: Moet + infinitive makes wachten the final verb, nog says the wait remains and even presents it as brief.

example.text: Wacht nog even op de bus.
example.english: Wait for the bus a little longer.

dutchnova1-0025.scenario: Your friend had planned to visit tomorrow. Check that the plan still stands.
dutchnova1-0025.explanation: Toch asks for confirmation of the expected visit; nog says the plan is still current.

example.text: Je komt morgen toch niet?
example.english: You're not coming tomorrow, are you?

dutchnova1-0025.english: You're not coming tomorrow, are you?
dutchnova1-0025.scenario: You expect your friend has cancelled tomorrow. Check your assumption.
dutchnova1-0025.explanation: Toch can still request confirmation, but niet reverses the expectation. This is not the same question as the parent card.

example.text: Je komt morgen toch nog?
example.english: You're still coming tomorrow, right?

dutchnova1-0026.text: Ik ben ziek, maar ik ga toch werken.
dutchnova1-0026.english: I'm ill, but I'm going to work anyway.
dutchnova1-0026.scenario: You feel ill but decide to go to work.
dutchnova1-0026.explanation: Toch expresses action despite a reason against it. Maar coordinates two main clauses; in the second one, ik remains the subject.

example.text: Het regent, maar ik ga toch voetballen.
example.english: It's raining, but I'm going to play football anyway.

dutchnova1-0026.text: Het regent, maar ik ga toch voetballen.
dutchnova1-0026.english: It's raining, but I'm going to play football anyway.
dutchnova1-0026.scenario: It's raining and a friend thinks you will cancel football, but you decide to go.
dutchnova1-0026.explanation: Toch counters the expectation created by the rain; gaan + infinitive puts voetballen at the end.

example.text: Ik ben ziek, maar ik ga toch werken.
example.english: I'm ill, but I'm going to work anyway.

dutchnova1-0029.scenario: Ask a sick friend whether they feel better today.
dutchnova1-0029.explanation: The first je is the subject; the second je is reflexive. Without the second je, this is not the usual form of zich voelen.

example.text: Je voelt je toch weer goed?
example.english: You're feeling well again, right?

dutchnova1-0029.text: Je voelt je toch weer goed?
dutchnova1-0029.scenario: You expect your friend to have recovered. Seek reassurance.
dutchnova1-0029.explanation: The subject je precedes voelt in a statement-shaped confirmation question. The next je is reflexive; toch asks for agreement and weer signals a restored state.

example.text: Voel je je vandaag beter?
example.english: Are you feeling better today?

dutchnova1-0033.text: We hadden samen voetbal moeten kijken.
dutchnova1-0033.english: We should have watched football together.
dutchnova1-0033.scenario: You regret missing a football night with friends.
dutchnova1-0033.explanation: Hadden + moeten + infinitive expresses hindsight or regret. Kijken remains an infinitive rather than the participle gekeken.

example.text: We moeten binnenkort eens afspreken.
example.english: We should arrange to meet sometime soon.

dutchnova1-0033.english: We should arrange to meet sometime soon.
dutchnova1-0033.scenario: You are suggesting a future get-together rather than regretting the past.
dutchnova1-0033.explanation: Moeten + infinitive is a direct present/future suggestion; compare hadden moeten for regret about an earlier missed opportunity.

example.text: We hadden samen voetbal moeten kijken.
example.english: We should have watched football together.

dutchnova1-0041.text: Ik heb het lekker warm onder de deken.
dutchnova1-0041.english: I'm comfortably warm under the blanket.
dutchnova1-0041.explanation: Het warm hebben expresses the person's comfort, not the room temperature. Lekker adds pleasantness; onder de deken indicates location.

example.text: Het wordt hier langzaam koud.
example.english: It's slowly getting cold here.

dutchnova1-0041.scenario: The heater has stopped working and the room temperature is dropping.
dutchnova1-0041.explanation: Wordt signals a change in the environmental condition, whereas het is koud would only describe the current temperature.

example.text: Ik heb het lekker warm onder de deken.
example.english: I'm comfortably warm under the blanket.

dutchnova1-0055.text: Als de server offline is, bel ik de beheerder.
dutchnova1-0055.english: If the server is offline, I'll call the administrator.
dutchnova1-0055.scenario: Your server is offline. Explain the action you take in that case.
dutchnova1-0055.explanation: The fronted als-clause ends with is; the following main clause has V2 inversion, bel ik, not ik bel.

example.text: Ik bel de beheerder als de server offline is.
example.english: I'll call the administrator if the server is offline.

dutchnova1-0055.text: Ik bel de beheerder als de server offline is.
dutchnova1-0055.english: I'll call the administrator if the server is offline.
dutchnova1-0055.scenario: You explain the same rule with the main clause first.
dutchnova1-0055.explanation: The main clause begins ik bel, so there is no inversion. The dependent als-clause still uses offline is.

example.text: Als de server offline is, bel ik de beheerder.
example.english: If the server is offline, I'll call the administrator.

dutchnova1-0098.text: Ik moet nog even naar de bakker.
dutchnova1-0098.english: I still need to pop to the baker's.
dutchnova1-0098.scenario: You are almost finished running errands, except buying bread.
dutchnova1-0098.explanation: Nog signals an unfinished errand, and even suggests a small trip. Naar de bakker is direction, not a present location.

example.text: Ik blijf nog even bij de bakker.
example.english: I'll stay at the bakery a little longer.

dutchnova1-0098.text: Ik blijf nog even bij de bakker.
dutchnova1-0098.english: I'll stay at the bakery a little longer.
dutchnova1-0098.scenario: You're already at the bakery and continue waiting for a friend.
dutchnova1-0098.explanation: Blijf denotes continued presence, so nog even means a little longer, not a remaining trip.

example.text: Ik moet nog even naar de bakker.
example.english: I still need to pop to the baker's.

dutchnova1-0117.text: Je voelt je toch al beter?
dutchnova1-0117.scenario: You expect a friend to have recovered. Check politely.
dutchnova1-0117.explanation: Je refers to the subject and the reflexive object separately. Toch signals expectation; al expresses recovery by now.

example.text: Ik voel me vandaag veel beter.
example.english: I feel much better today.

dutchnova1-0117.text: Ik voel me vandaag veel beter.
dutchnova1-0117.scenario: You recovered from a cold. Explain how you feel.
dutchnova1-0117.explanation: Zich voelen uses me with ik. Veel intensifies the comparative beter; vandaag supplies the time.

example.text: Je voelt je toch al beter?
example.english: You're feeling better already, right?

dutchnova1-0046.text: Ik probeer de deur niet aan te raken.
dutchnova1-0046.english: I'm trying not to touch the door.
dutchnova1-0046.scenario: The door has wet paint. Explain you're avoiding touching it.
dutchnova1-0046.explanation: Aanraken is separable. After proberen, te is inserted inside the verb: aan te raken. Niet negates the touching.

example.text: Raak dat scherm niet aan.
example.english: Don't touch that screen.

dutchnova1-0046.scenario: A child is about to touch a monitor. Tell them not to.
dutchnova1-0046.explanation: Raak ... aan is the imperative form of aanraken: the separable particle comes later in the clause.

example.text: Ik probeer de deur niet aan te raken.
example.english: I'm trying not to touch the door.

dutchnova1-0056.text: Kun je even controleren of de printer werkt?
dutchnova1-0056.english: Could you quickly check whether the printer works?
dutchnova1-0056.scenario: A colleague reports a printer issue. Ask someone to test it.
dutchnova1-0056.explanation: Of introduces an indirect yes/no question, so werkt follows de printer. Even softens the request.

example.text: Als de printer niet werkt, bel ik IT.
example.english: If the printer doesn't work, I'll call IT.

dutchnova1-0056.text: Als de printer niet werkt, bel ik IT.
dutchnova1-0056.english: If the printer doesn't work, I'll call IT.
dutchnova1-0056.scenario: Explain what you will do if the printer fails.
dutchnova1-0056.explanation: Als introduces a condition, not an indirect question. Fronting the clause causes bel ik inversion.

example.text: Kun je even controleren of de printer werkt?
example.english: Could you quickly check whether the printer works?

dutchnova1-0068.text: Moet je de dokter morgen nog bellen?
dutchnova1-0068.english: Do you still have to call the doctor tomorrow?
dutchnova1-0068.scenario: Your friend planned to phone the doctor tomorrow. Check whether they still need to.
dutchnova1-0068.explanation: Moet introduces necessity, nog means the task remains and bellen is the final infinitive.

example.text: Heb je de dokter al gebeld?
example.english: Have you already called the doctor?

dutchnova1-0068.text: Heb je de dokter al gebeld?
dutchnova1-0068.english: Have you already called the doctor?
dutchnova1-0068.scenario: Ask if the call you discussed has already happened.
dutchnova1-0068.explanation: Al checks completed status; heb + gebeld forms the perfect. This is not equivalent to asking whether the call is still required.

example.text: Moet je de dokter morgen nog bellen?
example.english: Do you still have to call the doctor tomorrow?

dutchnova1-0150.text: Ik kijk graag naar tennis, maar ik speel liever voetbal.
dutchnova1-0150.english: I enjoy watching tennis, but I prefer playing football.
dutchnova1-0150.scenario: You enjoy watching tennis, but when you play a sport you prefer football.
dutchnova1-0150.explanation: Graag describes enjoyment of watching; liever contrasts a stronger preference for actually playing football. Naar is the fixed preposition of kijken naar. These are preferences about different activities, not equivalent sentences.

example.text: Ik kijk graag naar voetbal, maar ik speel liever.
example.english: I enjoy watching football, but I prefer playing.

dutchnova1-0150.text: Ik kijk graag naar voetbal, maar ik speel liever.
dutchnova1-0150.english: I enjoy watching football, but I prefer playing.
dutchnova1-0150.scenario: You enjoy both watching and playing football, but playing is your preference.
dutchnova1-0150.explanation: Graag denotes enjoyment and liever denotes preference. They are not equivalents: the second choice outranks the first.

example.text: Ik kijk graag naar tennis, maar ik speel liever voetbal.
example.english: I enjoy watching tennis, but I prefer playing football.

dutchnova1-0002.text: We moeten alleen nog brood kopen.
dutchnova1-0002.english: We only still need to buy bread.
dutchnova1-0002.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We only still need to buy bread.
dutchnova1-0002.explanation: Alleen nog identifies bread as the one remaining shopping task; moeten + kopen names the required action rather than using a shopping-list fragment. Compare the base expression: Nu alleen nog een lekker stukje vlees. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted alleen nog pattern.

example.text: Nu alleen nog een lekker stukje vlees.
example.english: Everything is ready for dinner except a piece of meat.

dutchnova1-0004.text: Mag ik een andere maat proberen?
dutchnova1-0004.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: May I try another size?
dutchnova1-0004.explanation: Een andere maat shifts the object from coat to size, keeping the -e adjective with the de-word maat and the modal question construction. Compare the base expression: Mag ik een andere jas passen? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted een andere pattern.

example.text: Mag ik een andere jas passen?
example.english: The first coat did not fit. Ask to try a different coat.

dutchnova1-0005.text: Kan ik de andere schoenen even passen?
dutchnova1-0005.english: Can I quickly try the other shoes on?
dutchnova1-0005.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Can I quickly try the other shoes on?
dutchnova1-0005.explanation: De andere refers to one identifiable alternative among the shoes. Even softens the fitting request; passen is the final infinitive after kan. Compare the base expression: Mag ik de andere jas passen? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted de andere pattern.

example.text: Mag ik de andere jas passen?
example.english: You saw two coats and now want the other specific one.

dutchnova1-0006.text: Heeft u nog een andere kleur?
dutchnova1-0006.english: Do you have another different color?
dutchnova1-0006.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Do you have another different color?
dutchnova1-0006.explanation: Nog een andere requests an additional distinct option; kleur is a de-word, so andere takes -e. Heeft u is a formal shop question. Compare the base expression: Heb je nog een andere jas? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted nog een andere pattern.

example.text: Heb je nog een andere jas?
example.english: You have already tried several coats; ask for yet another different one.

dutchnova1-0007.text: Dan krijg je nog twee euro terug.
dutchnova1-0007.english: Then you get another two euros back.
dutchnova1-0007.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Then you get another two euros back.
dutchnova1-0007.explanation: Starting with dan requires krijg before je; terug is the separable particle of terugkrijgen. The situation is informal, unlike the parent card's u. Compare the base expression: Dan krijgt u nog drie euro terug. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted wisselgeld pattern.

example.text: Dan krijgt u nog drie euro terug.
example.english: A cashier politely tells a customer they will get three euros back.

dutchnova1-0008.text: Die appels zijn vandaag in de aanbieding.
dutchnova1-0008.english: Those apples are on offer today.
dutchnova1-0008.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Those apples are on offer today.
dutchnova1-0008.explanation: Die modifies plural appels, and plural zijn agrees with it. In de aanbieding is the fixed phrase for a sale. Compare the base expression: De uien zijn in de aanbieding. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted aanbieding pattern.

example.text: De uien zijn in de aanbieding.
example.english: Tell your friend that onions are on special offer.

dutchnova1-0009.text: Krijg ik korting op deze jas?
dutchnova1-0009.english: Do I get a discount on this coat?
dutchnova1-0009.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Do I get a discount on this coat?
dutchnova1-0009.explanation: Korting op is the fixed combination and deze goes with the de-word jas. Question inversion puts krijg before ik. Compare the base expression: Is er korting op de uien? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted korting pattern.

example.text: Is er korting op de uien?
example.english: Ask if there is a discount on the onions.

dutchnova1-0010.text: Ik heb de appels gekocht omdat ze goedkoper waren.
dutchnova1-0010.english: I bought the apples because they were cheaper.
dutchnova1-0010.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I bought the apples because they were cheaper.
dutchnova1-0010.explanation: Omdat gives the reason and sends waren to the end; cheaper is expressed with the comparative goedkoper. Compare the base expression: Ik heb aardappelen gekocht omdat ze in promotie waren. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted aanbieding pattern.

example.text: Ik heb aardappelen gekocht omdat ze in promotie waren.
example.english: Explain that you bought potatoes because they were on promotion.

dutchnova1-0013.text: Ik drink liever water dan frisdrank.
dutchnova1-0013.english: I prefer drinking water to soft drinks.
dutchnova1-0013.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I prefer drinking water to soft drinks.
dutchnova1-0013.explanation: Liever ... dan compares the two drinks, and the present-tense verb drink comes after ik. Compare the base expression: Ik eet liever kip dan vis. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted liever pattern.

example.text: Ik eet liever kip dan vis.
example.english: Say you prefer chicken to fish.

dutchnova1-0014.text: Ik eet het liefst rijst met kip.
dutchnova1-0014.english: I prefer rice with chicken most of all.
dutchnova1-0014.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I prefer rice with chicken most of all.
dutchnova1-0014.explanation: Het liefst names a strongest preference rather than a two-option comparison; the meal has a different ingredient order. Compare the base expression: Ik eet het liefst kip met rijst. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted het liefst pattern.

example.text: Ik eet het liefst kip met rijst.
example.english: Explain that chicken with rice is your favourite thing to eat.

dutchnova1-0015.text: Ik lust geen paprika, maar wel tomaten.
dutchnova1-0015.english: I dislike peppers but do like tomatoes.
dutchnova1-0015.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I dislike peppers but do like tomatoes.
dutchnova1-0015.explanation: Geen negates the general food preference; wel makes the positive contrast with the next food explicit. Compare the base expression: Ik lust geen uien. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted niet vs geen pattern.

example.text: Ik lust geen uien.
example.english: Tell your friend you do not like onions.

dutchnova1-0016.text: Mag ik een klein stukje cake?
dutchnova1-0016.english: May I have a small piece of cake?
dutchnova1-0016.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: May I have a small piece of cake?
dutchnova1-0016.explanation: Klein has no -e because stukje is a singular indefinite het-word, even though cake is a de-word in other constructions. Compare the base expression: Mag ik een stukje taart? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted stukje pattern.

example.text: Mag ik een stukje taart?
example.english: Ask for a small piece of cake.

dutchnova1-0017.text: Ik wil graag een warm stukje vlees.
dutchnova1-0017.english: I'd like a warm piece of meat.
dutchnova1-0017.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'd like a warm piece of meat.
dutchnova1-0017.explanation: Warm is uninflected before een stukje (singular indefinite het-word); wil graag makes a polite preference statement. Compare the base expression: Mag ik een lekker stukje vlees? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted adjective pattern.

example.text: Mag ik een lekker stukje vlees?
example.english: Ask for a tasty little piece of meat.

dutchnova1-0018.text: We hebben drie Nederlandse films gezien.
dutchnova1-0018.english: We have watched three Dutch films.
dutchnova1-0018.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We have watched three Dutch films.
dutchnova1-0018.explanation: Nederlandse takes -e before plural films. Gezien remains the past participle after hebben, but the number is now explicit. Compare the base expression: Ik heb een paar Spaanse series gezien. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted adjective pattern.

example.text: Ik heb een paar Spaanse series gezien.
example.english: Tell someone you watched a few Spanish series.

dutchnova1-0020.text: Ik heb vandaag nog geen koffie gedronken.
dutchnova1-0020.english: I haven't had any coffee today yet.
dutchnova1-0020.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I haven't had any coffee today yet.
dutchnova1-0020.explanation: Nog geen negates an unspecified amount of coffee; nog niet would more naturally negate the whole drinking event. Compare the base expression: Ik heb nog niet gegeten. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted nog niet pattern.

example.text: Ik heb nog niet gegeten.
example.english: Explain that you have not eaten yet.

dutchnova1-0021.text: Ben je nog steeds die serie aan het kijken?
dutchnova1-0021.english: Are you still watching that series?
dutchnova1-0021.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Are you still watching that series?
dutchnova1-0021.explanation: Aan het kijken describes the ongoing viewing; nog steeds asks about its surprising continuation. Die modifies de serie. Compare the base expression: Ben je nog steeds voetbal aan het kijken? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted nog steeds pattern.

example.text: Ben je nog steeds voetbal aan het kijken?
example.english: You are surprised your friend is still watching football.

dutchnova1-0023.text: Ik moet nog even mijn moeder terugbellen.
dutchnova1-0023.english: I still need to quickly call my mother back.
dutchnova1-0023.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I still need to quickly call my mother back.
dutchnova1-0023.explanation: Moet governs the whole infinitive terugbellen; nog even marks a small outstanding action and specifies the person. Compare the base expression: Ik moet nog even bellen. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted nog even pattern.

example.text: Ik moet nog even bellen.
example.english: Say you still need to make a quick call.

dutchnova1-0024.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: You've forgotten it again already!
dutchnova1-0024.explanation: Alweer expresses annoyed repetition; the participle vergeten is part of the perfect tense with hebt. Compare the base expression: Je vraagt het alweer! The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted alweer pattern.

example.text: Je vraagt het alweer!
example.english: Your friend has just asked the same question again.

dutchnova1-0027.text: We gaan toch niet naar de markt.
dutchnova1-0027.english: We're not going to the market after all.
dutchnova1-0027.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We're not going to the market after all.
dutchnova1-0027.explanation: Toch niet signals changed plans; gaan + destination states the cancelled movement rather than an invitation. Compare the base expression: Ik ga toch niet mee. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted toch after all pattern.

example.text: Ik ga toch niet mee.
example.english: You changed your mind: you are not coming after all.

dutchnova1-0030.text: Sorry, ik heb me in het adres vergist.
dutchnova1-0030.english: Sorry, I made a mistake about the address.
dutchnova1-0030.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Sorry, I made a mistake about the address.
dutchnova1-0030.explanation: Zich vergissen needs me with ik. In het adres makes the mistaken detail explicit. Compare the base expression: Ik heb me vergist. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted zich vergissen pattern.

example.text: Ik heb me vergist.
example.english: Admit you made a mistake.

dutchnova1-0031.text: Herinner je je dat gesprek nog?
dutchnova1-0031.english: Do you still remember that conversation?
dutchnova1-0031.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Do you still remember that conversation?
dutchnova1-0031.explanation: The first je is subject and the second reflexive; nog asks whether the memory remains. Dat modifies the het-word gesprek. Compare the base expression: Herinner je je onze voetbalwedstrijd nog? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted zich herinneren pattern.

example.text: Herinner je je onze voetbalwedstrijd nog?
example.english: Ask a friend whether they still remember your old football game.

dutchnova1-0032.text: We zouden volgende week eens kunnen afspreken.
dutchnova1-0032.english: We could arrange to meet sometime next week.
dutchnova1-0032.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We could arrange to meet sometime next week.
dutchnova1-0032.explanation: Zouden + kunnen + afspreken softens a suggested meeting. Volgende week gives a different time. Compare the base expression: We zouden binnenkort eens moeten afspreken. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted zou pattern.

example.text: We zouden binnenkort eens moeten afspreken.
example.english: Suggest meeting up sometime soon.

dutchnova1-0034.text: We hadden moeten afspreken om samen te koken.
dutchnova1-0034.english: We should have arranged to meet to cook together.
dutchnova1-0034.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We should have arranged to meet to cook together.
dutchnova1-0034.explanation: Hadden moeten + afspreken expresses hindsight; om ... te koken states the missed meeting's purpose. Compare the base expression: We hadden moeten afspreken om samen voetbal te kijken. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted om te pattern.

example.text: We hadden moeten afspreken om samen voetbal te kijken.
example.english: Say you should have met up to watch football.

dutchnova1-0035.text: Kijk je vanavond nog iets op Netflix?
dutchnova1-0035.english: Are you watching anything on Netflix tonight?
dutchnova1-0035.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Are you watching anything on Netflix tonight?
dutchnova1-0035.explanation: Nog asks whether an additional or outstanding viewing is planned; iets is the unspecified object, and op Netflix marks the platform. Compare the base expression: Kijk je iets op tv? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted iets pattern.

example.text: Kijk je iets op tv?
example.english: Ask whether someone is watching anything on TV.

dutchnova1-0036.text: Wat ben je op dit moment aan het lezen?
dutchnova1-0036.english: What are you reading at the moment?
dutchnova1-0036.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: What are you reading at the moment?
dutchnova1-0036.explanation: Aan het lezen uses the same progressive structure, now with the reading activity and a more explicit time phrase. Compare the base expression: Wat ben je nu aan het doen? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted aan het pattern.

example.text: Wat ben je nu aan het doen?
example.english: Ask what someone is doing right now.

dutchnova1-0037.text: Ik heb beide series op Netflix gezien.
dutchnova1-0037.english: I've watched both series on Netflix.
dutchnova1-0037.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I've watched both series on Netflix.
dutchnova1-0037.explanation: Beide modifies plural series before its noun, contrasting with allebei after the two titles in the parent. Compare the base expression: Ik heb Money Heist en Elite allebei gezien. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted allebei pattern.

example.text: Ik heb Money Heist en Elite allebei gezien.
example.english: Say you have seen both Money Heist and Elite.

dutchnova1-0040.text: Zou je eerder gaan slapen als je morgen moest werken?
dutchnova1-0040.english: Would you go to sleep earlier if you had to work tomorrow?
dutchnova1-0040.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Would you go to sleep earlier if you had to work tomorrow?
dutchnova1-0040.explanation: Zou ... gaan slapen asks hypothetically; als introduces a condition ending with moest werken. Compare the base expression: Hoe laat zou je gaan slapen als je morgen vrij was? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted conditional zou pattern.

example.text: Hoe laat zou je gaan slapen als je morgen vrij was?
example.english: Ask what time someone would go to bed if tomorrow were free.

dutchnova1-0042.text: Ik krijg het warm zodra de zon schijnt.
dutchnova1-0042.english: I start feeling warm as soon as the sun shines.
dutchnova1-0042.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I start feeling warm as soon as the sun shines.
dutchnova1-0042.explanation: Krijg het warm marks the onset of a sensation, and zodra introduces a time clause with schijnt in final position. Compare the base expression: Ik krijg het koud. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted krijg het koud pattern.

example.text: Ik krijg het koud.
example.english: Tell someone you're starting to feel cold.

dutchnova1-0043.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: It's slowly getting warmer here.
dutchnova1-0043.explanation: Wordt expresses a change rather than a static condition; warmer is the comparative of warm. Compare the base expression: Het is lekker warm hier. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted lekker warm pattern.

example.text: Het is lekker warm hier.
example.english: Say the room feels pleasantly warm.

dutchnova1-0044.text: Die koffie is nog lekker warm.
dutchnova1-0044.english: That coffee is still pleasantly warm.
dutchnova1-0044.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: That coffee is still pleasantly warm.
dutchnova1-0044.explanation: Die can refer to de koffie; nog means the earlier temperature continues, not that the surrounding room is warm. Compare the base expression: De koffie is lekker warm. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted de/het pronoun pattern.

example.text: De koffie is lekker warm.
example.english: You are holding a warm cup of coffee; tell a friend it is pleasantly warm.

dutchnova1-0045.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Don't touch that cable!
dutchnova1-0045.explanation: Raak ... aan splits the imperative of aanraken, and dat goes with the singular het-word snoer. Compare the base expression: Raak de hete pan niet aan. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted aanraken pattern.

example.text: Raak de hete pan niet aan.
example.english: Tell a child not to touch the hot pan.

dutchnova1-0047.text: Ik ruik verse koffie in de keuken.
dutchnova1-0047.english: I can smell fresh coffee in the kitchen.
dutchnova1-0047.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I can smell fresh coffee in the kitchen.
dutchnova1-0047.explanation: Ruik is present tense of ruiken; verse modifies de koffie with -e, and in de keuken gives the location. Compare the base expression: Ik ruik rook in de keuken. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted ruiken pattern.

example.text: Ik ruik rook in de keuken.
example.english: Say you smell smoke in the kitchen.

dutchnova1-0048.text: Ik rook vorige week gas in de kelder.
dutchnova1-0048.english: I smelled gas in the basement last week.
dutchnova1-0048.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I smelled gas in the basement last week.
dutchnova1-0048.explanation: Rook is past tense of ruiken, not a reference to tobacco here; vorige week establishes a clear past setting. Compare the base expression: Ik rook gisteren iets vreemds. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted rook past pattern.

example.text: Ik rook gisteren iets vreemds.
example.english: Say you smelled something strange yesterday.

dutchnova1-0049.text: Na een lange dag word ik moe.
dutchnova1-0049.english: After a long day, I start feeling tired.
dutchnova1-0049.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: After a long day, I start feeling tired.
dutchnova1-0049.explanation: The fronted time phrase causes word-second inversion, word ik; word (without -t) remains the first-person form. Compare the base expression: Ik word moe. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted worden pattern.

example.text: Ik word moe.
example.english: Say you are becoming tired.

dutchnova1-0050.text: Ik ga op de bank zitten.
dutchnova1-0050.english: I'm going to sit down on the sofa.
dutchnova1-0050.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'm going to sit down on the sofa.
dutchnova1-0050.explanation: Gaan zitten describes movement into a seated position, contrasting with already being seated: ik zit. Compare the base expression: Ik zit op een stoel. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted zitten pattern.

example.text: Ik zit op een stoel.
example.english: Tell someone you are sitting on a chair.

dutchnova1-0051.text: Ik blijf nog even bij mijn vrienden.
dutchnova1-0051.english: I'll stay with my friends a little longer.
dutchnova1-0051.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'll stay with my friends a little longer.
dutchnova1-0051.explanation: Nog even extends an existing visit; bij shows being with people rather than going toward them. Compare the base expression: Ik blijf nog even hier. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted blijven pattern.

example.text: Ik blijf nog even hier.
example.english: Say you are staying here for a little longer.

dutchnova1-0052.text: Ik werk in IT en ik leer Nederlands.
dutchnova1-0052.english: I work in IT and I'm learning Dutch.
dutchnova1-0052.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I work in IT and I'm learning Dutch.
dutchnova1-0052.explanation: Two independent clauses connected by en each have a finite verb after the subject; the second describes language learning. Compare the base expression: Ik ben system engineer en ik zoek momenteel een job. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted job pattern.

example.text: Ik ben system engineer en ik zoek momenteel een job.
example.english: Say you are a system engineer and currently looking for a job.

dutchnova1-0053.text: Terwijl ik thuis werk, oefen ik Nederlandse zinnen.
dutchnova1-0053.english: While I work from home, I practise Dutch sentences.
dutchnova1-0053.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: While I work from home, I practise Dutch sentences.
dutchnova1-0053.explanation: Terwijl's dependent verb werk comes at clause end, and fronting it requires oefen ik in the main clause. Compare the base expression: Terwijl ik Nederlands leer, blijf ik mijn IT-skills ontwikkelen. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted terwijl pattern.

example.text: Terwijl ik Nederlands leer, blijf ik mijn IT-skills ontwikkelen.
example.english: While learning Dutch, you are continuing to develop IT skills.

dutchnova1-0054.text: Omdat de printer vastloopt, bel ik de helpdesk.
dutchnova1-0054.english: Because the printer jams, I call the helpdesk.
dutchnova1-0054.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Because the printer jams, I call the helpdesk.
dutchnova1-0054.explanation: The subordinate clause with omdat ends in vastloopt; the main verb bel is inverted before ik after the fronted cause. Compare the base expression: Omdat de server niet reageert, controleer ik de logs. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted omdat pattern.

example.text: Omdat de server niet reageert, controleer ik de logs.
example.english: Explain that you check the logs because the server is unresponsive.

dutchnova1-0057.text: Ik vraag even wanneer het gesprek begint.
dutchnova1-0057.english: I'll quickly ask when the meeting starts.
dutchnova1-0057.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'll quickly ask when the meeting starts.
dutchnova1-0057.explanation: Wanneer introduces an indirect question, so the finite verb begint follows het gesprek rather than preceding it. Compare the base expression: Ik kijk even wanneer de vergadering begint. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted wanneer pattern.

example.text: Ik kijk even wanneer de vergadering begint.
example.english: Say you're checking when the meeting starts.

dutchnova1-0058.text: Ik moet de configuratie nog afmaken.
dutchnova1-0058.english: I still have to finish the configuration.
dutchnova1-0058.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I still have to finish the configuration.
dutchnova1-0058.explanation: Moet takes infinitive afmaken at the end and nog marks the unfinished item; the object is changed to an IT configuration. Compare the base expression: Ik moet het verslag nog afmaken. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted nog pattern.

example.text: Ik moet het verslag nog afmaken.
example.english: Tell your colleague you still have to finish the report.

dutchnova1-0059.text: Morgen ga ik meteen naar kantoor.
dutchnova1-0059.english: Tomorrow I'll go straight to the office.
dutchnova1-0059.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Tomorrow I'll go straight to the office.
dutchnova1-0059.explanation: Fronted morgen triggers ga ik inversion and meteen means immediately rather than usually. Compare the base expression: Na het werk ga ik meteen naar huis. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted inversion pattern.

example.text: Na het werk ga ik meteen naar huis.
example.english: Say you are going home immediately after work.

dutchnova1-0060.text: Kunnen we volgende week een afspraak maken?
dutchnova1-0060.english: Could we make an appointment next week?
dutchnova1-0060.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Could we make an appointment next week?
dutchnova1-0060.explanation: Een afspraak maken names the appointment as an object; it contrasts with afspreken, agreeing to meet. Compare the base expression: Kunnen we morgen even afspreken? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted afspreken pattern.

example.text: Kunnen we morgen even afspreken?
example.english: Ask to arrange a meeting with your colleague tomorrow.

dutchnova1-0061.text: Ik bereid me voor op het technisch interview.
dutchnova1-0061.english: I'm preparing myself for the technical interview.
dutchnova1-0061.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'm preparing myself for the technical interview.
dutchnova1-0061.explanation: Me is reflexive with ik, the separable verb is bereid ... voor, and op indicates the thing prepared for. Compare the base expression: Ik bereid me voor op mijn sollicitatiegesprek. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted voorbereiden pattern.

example.text: Ik bereid me voor op mijn sollicitatiegesprek.
example.english: Say you're preparing for a job interview.

dutchnova1-0062.text: Ik houd de documentatie elke week bij.
dutchnova1-0062.english: I keep the documentation updated every week.
dutchnova1-0062.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I keep the documentation updated every week.
dutchnova1-0062.explanation: The separable verb bijhouden becomes houd ... bij; elke week marks a recurring habit. Compare the base expression: Ik houd mijn technische kennis bij. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted bijhouden pattern.

example.text: Ik houd mijn technische kennis bij.
example.english: Explain that you keep your technical knowledge up to date.

dutchnova1-0063.text: Heb je hulp nodig bij de installatie?
dutchnova1-0063.english: Do you need help with the installation?
dutchnova1-0063.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Do you need help with the installation?
dutchnova1-0063.explanation: Nodig hebben governs the noun hulp; bij marks the activity in which help is needed, and inversion gives heb je. Compare the base expression: Ik heb hulp nodig met het netwerk. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted nodig pattern.

example.text: Ik heb hulp nodig met het netwerk.
example.english: Say you need help with the network.

dutchnova1-0064.text: Je hoeft de router vandaag niet te herstarten.
dutchnova1-0064.english: You don't need to restart the router today.
dutchnova1-0064.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: You don't need to restart the router today.
dutchnova1-0064.explanation: Hoeven requires te before herstarten and the negation niet says there is no necessity, not a prohibition. Compare the base expression: Je hoeft de server niet meer opnieuw op te starten. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted hoeven pattern.

example.text: Je hoeft de server niet meer opnieuw op te starten.
example.english: Tell a colleague they no longer need to restart the server.

dutchnova1-0065.text: Ik heb de back-up al nagekeken.
dutchnova1-0065.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I've already checked the backup.
dutchnova1-0065.explanation: Nagekeken is the past participle of nakijken, with prefix and participle joined; al means completed by now. Compare the base expression: Ik heb de logs al gecontroleerd. The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted perfect pattern.

example.text: Ik heb de logs al gecontroleerd.
example.english: Tell a colleague you have already checked the logs.

dutchnova1-0066.text: Tegen wanneer moet ik dit formulier indienen?
dutchnova1-0066.english: By when must I submit this form?
dutchnova1-0066.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: By when must I submit this form?
dutchnova1-0066.explanation: Tegen wanneer asks a deadline, and dit modifies the singular het-word formulier; indienen follows the modal moet. Compare the base expression: Wanneer moet ik deze opdracht indienen? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted vragen pattern.

example.text: Wanneer moet ik deze opdracht indienen?
example.english: Ask when you have to submit the assignment.

dutchnova1-0067.text: Je hebt de nieuwe link toch gezien?
dutchnova1-0067.english: You did see the new link, right?
dutchnova1-0067.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: You did see the new link, right?
dutchnova1-0067.explanation: Toch asks for confirmation of an expected event. Gezien is the participle of zien; nieuwe takes -e with de link. Compare the base expression: Je hebt mijn mail toch gekregen? The new sentence changes the situation while keeping the targeted toch pattern.

example.text: Je hebt mijn mail toch gekregen?
example.english: You expect the colleague to have received your email; check politely.

dutchnova1-0069.text: Hoef je je tandarts morgen nog te bellen?
dutchnova1-0069.english: Do you still need to call your dentist tomorrow?
dutchnova1-0069.scenario: At an appointment, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Do you still need to call your dentist tomorrow?
dutchnova1-0069.explanation: Hoef + te bellen asks whether the task is necessary; nog keeps the obligation open. The base sentence is Hoef je de dokter vandaag nog te bellen?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Hoef je de dokter vandaag nog te bellen?
example.english: Ask whether a friend still needs to phone the doctor today.

dutchnova1-0070.text: Zou het mogelijk zijn om een andere afspraak te maken?
dutchnova1-0070.english: Would it be possible to make another appointment?
dutchnova1-0070.scenario: At an appointment, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Would it be possible to make another appointment?
dutchnova1-0070.explanation: Zou ... zijn forms a polite hypothetical request; om ... te maken names the requested action. The base sentence is Zou het mogelijk zijn om Engels te spreken?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Zou het mogelijk zijn om Engels te spreken?
example.english: On the phone, politely ask whether it's possible to speak English.

dutchnova1-0071.text: Ik wil graag een afspraak maken voor volgende week.
dutchnova1-0071.english: I'd like to arrange an appointment for next week.
dutchnova1-0071.scenario: At an appointment, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'd like to arrange an appointment for next week.
dutchnova1-0071.explanation: Een afspraak maken stays as a noun-verb pair, and graag makes the request polite. The base sentence is Ik wil graag een afspraak maken bij de dokter.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik wil graag een afspraak maken bij de dokter.
example.english: Say you want to make an appointment with the doctor.

dutchnova1-0072.text: Als het morgen regent, ga je dan nog voetballen?
dutchnova1-0072.english: If it rains tomorrow, will you still play football?
dutchnova1-0072.scenario: In a football situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: If it rains tomorrow, will you still play football?
dutchnova1-0072.explanation: The conditional als-clause sends regent to the end and fronting it triggers ga je; dan makes the response to the condition explicit. The base sentence is Als het regent, zou je dan nog naar de sportschool gaan?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Als het regent, zou je dan nog naar de sportschool gaan?
example.english: If it rains, ask whether a friend would still go to the gym.

dutchnova1-0073.text: We verliezen, maar we blijven toch spelen.
dutchnova1-0073.english: We're losing, but we'll keep playing anyway.
dutchnova1-0073.scenario: In a football situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We're losing, but we'll keep playing anyway.
dutchnova1-0073.explanation: Toch contrasts with the bad score; blijven + infinitive spelen expresses continuation. The base sentence is We staan achter, maar ik blijf toch kijken.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: We staan achter, maar ik blijf toch kijken.
example.english: Your team is losing, but you will watch the match anyway.

dutchnova1-0074.text: Ik zoek iemand om vanavond mee te gamen.
dutchnova1-0074.english: I'm looking for someone to game with tonight.
dutchnova1-0074.scenario: In a football situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'm looking for someone to game with tonight.
dutchnova1-0074.explanation: Om ... mee te gamen expresses the purpose of finding a gaming partner. Mee marks together-with. The base sentence is Ik zoek iemand om FIFA mee te spelen.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik zoek iemand om FIFA mee te spelen.
example.english: Say you are looking for someone to play FIFA with.

dutchnova1-0075.scenario: In a football situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: What a beautiful cross!
dutchnova1-0075.explanation: Voorzet is a de-word, so the adjective mooie takes -e after een, unlike mooi with het doelpunt. The base sentence is Wat een mooi doelpunt!; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Wat een mooi doelpunt!
example.english: React to a surprisingly beautiful goal.

dutchnova1-0076.text: Ik ben er over ongeveer een halfuur.
dutchnova1-0076.english: I'll be there in about half an hour.
dutchnova1-0076.scenario: In a travel situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'll be there in about half an hour.
dutchnova1-0076.explanation: Over gives a future interval, ongeveer makes it approximate; er marks the destination already known. The base sentence is Ik kom over ongeveer tien minuten.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik kom over ongeveer tien minuten.
example.english: Tell a friend you'll arrive in about ten minutes.

dutchnova1-0077.english: I'll pop by a little later.
dutchnova1-0077.scenario: In a travel situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'll pop by a little later.
dutchnova1-0077.explanation: Straks locates the future visit, even suggests it will be brief, and langskomen separates as kom ... langs. The base sentence is Ik bel je straks.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik bel je straks.
example.english: Say you'll call your friend later today.

dutchnova1-0078.text: Ik heb haar daarnet op het station gezien.
dutchnova1-0078.english: I saw her at the station a little while ago.
dutchnova1-0078.scenario: In a travel situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I saw her at the station a little while ago.
dutchnova1-0078.explanation: Daarnet gives recent past; heb ... gezien is the completed perfect tense. The base sentence is Ik heb de bus daarnet gezien.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb de bus daarnet gezien.
example.english: Say you saw the bus just a little while ago.

dutchnova1-0079.text: Er vertrekt over tien minuten nog een trein.
dutchnova1-0079.english: Another train leaves in ten minutes.
dutchnova1-0079.scenario: In a travel situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Another train leaves in ten minutes.
dutchnova1-0079.explanation: Er introduces an available service; nog een indicates an extra departure, and over measures time from now. The base sentence is Er is over een kwartier nog een bus.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Er is over een kwartier nog een bus.
example.english: Tell your friend there is another bus in fifteen minutes.

dutchnova1-0080.text: De auto die voor het huis staat, is van mij.
dutchnova1-0080.english: The car that's parked in front of the house is mine.
dutchnova1-0080.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: The car that's parked in front of the house is mine.
dutchnova1-0080.explanation: Die is the relative pronoun for the de-word auto and staat closes the relative clause. The base sentence is Het huis dat te koop staat, is heel duur.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Het huis dat te koop staat, is heel duur.
example.english: Tell someone the house that's for sale is very expensive.

dutchnova1-0081.text: Ik probeer het probleem vandaag op te lossen.
dutchnova1-0081.english: I'm trying to solve the problem today.
dutchnova1-0081.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'm trying to solve the problem today.
dutchnova1-0081.explanation: Oplossen is separable and after proberen takes op te lossen, with te inserted between particle and stem. The base sentence is Ik heb een oplossing voor het probleem gevonden.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb een oplossing voor het probleem gevonden.
example.english: Say you've found a solution to the problem.

dutchnova1-0082.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: What a romantic moment!
dutchnova1-0082.explanation: Wat een introduces a noun exclamation; romantisch stays without -e before an indefinite singular het-word moment. The base sentence is Wat romantisch!; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Wat romantisch!
example.english: React to a romantic surprise.

dutchnova1-0083.text: Deze avond is nog gezelliger dan gisteren.
dutchnova1-0083.english: This evening is even cosier than yesterday.
dutchnova1-0083.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: This evening is even cosier than yesterday.
dutchnova1-0083.explanation: Nog boosts comparative gezelliger; dan introduces the reference point of comparison. The base sentence is Dit is nog romantischer.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Dit is nog romantischer.
example.english: Say this is even more romantic.

dutchnova1-0084.text: Ze heeft het probleem zelf opgelost.
dutchnova1-0084.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: She solved the problem herself.
dutchnova1-0084.explanation: Zelf emphasizes who did it, without acting as reflexive zich; opgelost is the participle of oplossen. The base sentence is Ik heb de taak zelf afgemaakt.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb de taak zelf afgemaakt.
example.english: Tell your manager you completed the task yourself.

dutchnova1-0085.text: Ik ben de keuken aan het schoonmaken.
dutchnova1-0085.english: I'm cleaning the kitchen at the moment.
dutchnova1-0085.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'm cleaning the kitchen at the moment.
dutchnova1-0085.explanation: Aan het schoonmaken emphasizes an ongoing action and concerns cleaning, not necessarily putting things away. The base sentence is Ik ben mijn kamer aan het opruimen.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik ben mijn kamer aan het opruimen.
example.english: Tell someone you are tidying your room right now.

dutchnova1-0086.text: We hebben de woonkamer eindelijk opgeruimd.
dutchnova1-0086.english: We've finally tidied the living room.
dutchnova1-0086.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We've finally tidied the living room.
dutchnova1-0086.explanation: Opgeruimd is the completed participle; eindelijk comments that the completion came after some delay. The base sentence is Ik heb mijn kamer opgeruimd.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb mijn kamer opgeruimd.
example.english: Say you have finished tidying your room.

dutchnova1-0087.text: Kan ik je morgen even terugbellen?
dutchnova1-0087.english: Can I call you back briefly tomorrow?
dutchnova1-0087.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Can I call you back briefly tomorrow?
dutchnova1-0087.explanation: Terugbellen stays joined after modal kan; even softens the request and morgen changes the time. The base sentence is Kun je me straks terugbellen?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Kun je me straks terugbellen?
example.english: Ask someone to call you back shortly.

dutchnova1-0088.text: Ik ben net even naar de bakker geweest.
dutchnova1-0088.english: I've just popped to the baker's.
dutchnova1-0088.scenario: In a home situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I've just popped to the baker's.
dutchnova1-0088.explanation: Net says the errand just happened; even presents the visit as brief. Ben ... geweest is the perfect of zijn. The base sentence is Ik heb net even iets gegeten.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb net even iets gegeten.
example.english: Say you just ate a quick bite.

dutchnova1-0089.text: We hebben nog maar twee tickets.
dutchnova1-0089.english: We only have two tickets left.
dutchnova1-0089.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We only have two tickets left.
dutchnova1-0089.explanation: Nog maar emphasizes a limited remaining quantity rather than merely stating two are available. The base sentence is Ik heb nog maar vijf euro.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb nog maar vijf euro.
example.english: Tell someone you only have five euros left.

dutchnova1-0090.text: Ik kijk die serie niet meer.
dutchnova1-0090.english: I don't watch that series anymore.
dutchnova1-0090.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I don't watch that series anymore.
dutchnova1-0090.explanation: Niet meer says an earlier viewing habit has ended; this differs from nog niet, which means not yet. The base sentence is Ik ben niet meer boos.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik ben niet meer boos.
example.english: Tell someone you're no longer angry.

dutchnova1-0091.text: Mijn broer wil de wedstrijd ook kijken.
dutchnova1-0091.english: My brother wants to watch the match too.
dutchnova1-0091.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: My brother wants to watch the match too.
dutchnova1-0091.explanation: Ook marks an additional viewer or action; the modal wil sends kijken to the final position. The base sentence is Ik wil ook de wedstrijd kijken.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik wil ook de wedstrijd kijken.
example.english: Tell a friend you also want to watch the match.

dutchnova1-0092.text: Met de verzendkosten erbij kost het twintig euro.
dutchnova1-0092.english: With shipping costs included, it costs twenty euros.
dutchnova1-0092.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: With shipping costs included, it costs twenty euros.
dutchnova1-0092.explanation: Erbij signals adding an extra to the total. The opening phrase triggers inversion kost het. The base sentence is Met het zakje erbij is dat acht euro vijftig.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Met het zakje erbij is dat acht euro vijftig.
example.english: Cashier says including the bag, the total is eight euros fifty.

dutchnova1-0093.text: Kunnen we contactloos met de kaart betalen?
dutchnova1-0093.english: Can we pay contactlessly with a card?
dutchnova1-0093.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Can we pay contactlessly with a card?
dutchnova1-0093.explanation: Kunnen opens a yes/no modal question, met de kaart identifies payment method, and betalen is the final infinitive. The base sentence is Kan ik met de kaart betalen?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Kan ik met de kaart betalen?
example.english: Ask the cashier whether you can pay by card.

dutchnova1-0094.text: Ik zou thuisgebleven zijn als het harder had geregend.
dutchnova1-0094.english: I would have stayed home if it had rained harder.
dutchnova1-0094.scenario: In a friends situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I would have stayed home if it had rained harder.
dutchnova1-0094.explanation: Zou ... zijn and past participle form a hypothetical past outcome; als ... had geregend expresses the unreal condition. The base sentence is Ik zou gegaan zijn als ik tijd had gehad.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik zou gegaan zijn als ik tijd had gehad.
example.english: Explain that you would have gone if you had had time.

dutchnova1-0095.text: Ik ben van plan om volgende week een cursus te volgen.
dutchnova1-0095.english: I plan to take a course next week.
dutchnova1-0095.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I plan to take a course next week.
dutchnova1-0095.explanation: Van plan zijn + om ... te expresses intention; the main activity volgen follows te. The base sentence is Ik ben van plan om morgen te solliciteren.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik ben van plan om morgen te solliciteren.
example.english: Say you're planning to apply for a job tomorrow.

dutchnova1-0096.text: We gaan na de pauze weer aan de slag.
dutchnova1-0096.english: We'll get back to work after the break.
dutchnova1-0096.scenario: At work, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We'll get back to work after the break.
dutchnova1-0096.explanation: Aan de slag gaan is idiomatic for starting work; weer says the work is being resumed. The base sentence is Ik ga meteen aan de slag.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik ga meteen aan de slag.
example.english: Say you're going to get started immediately.

dutchnova1-0097.text: Ik moet nog even melk kopen voordat de winkel sluit.
dutchnova1-0097.english: I still have to buy milk quickly before the shop closes.
dutchnova1-0097.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I still have to buy milk quickly before the shop closes.
dutchnova1-0097.explanation: Nog even marks the outstanding short errand, while voordat introduces a dependent clause ending with sluit. The base sentence is Ik moet nog even brood halen voordat de winkel sluit.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik moet nog even brood halen voordat de winkel sluit.
example.english: You are leaving home and have one quick errand left before the shops close.

dutchnova1-0099.text: Mag ik nog twee zakjes, alsjeblieft?
dutchnova1-0099.english: May I have two more bags, please?
dutchnova1-0099.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: May I have two more bags, please?
dutchnova1-0099.explanation: Nog expresses addition, two counts plural bags, and mag ik is a polite request. The base sentence is Mag ik nog een zakje, alsjeblieft?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Mag ik nog een zakje, alsjeblieft?
example.english: You already have one bag but ask the cashier for another one.

dutchnova1-0100.text: Ik heb alleen nog een pak melk nodig.
dutchnova1-0100.english: I only still need a carton of milk.
dutchnova1-0100.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I only still need a carton of milk.
dutchnova1-0100.explanation: Alleen nog limits what remains to one item; nodig hebben expresses need for a thing. The base sentence is Ik heb alleen nog eieren nodig.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb alleen nog eieren nodig.
example.english: You have bought everything except eggs.

dutchnova1-0101.text: Met de saus erbij is dat twaalf euro.
dutchnova1-0101.english: With the sauce included, that's twelve euros.
dutchnova1-0101.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: With the sauce included, that's twelve euros.
dutchnova1-0101.explanation: Erbij means added to a total and the fronted met-phrase forces is dat rather than dat is. The base sentence is Met het zakje erbij kost het negen euro.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Met het zakje erbij kost het negen euro.
example.english: The shop assistant says the total includes the extra bag.

dutchnova1-0102.text: Kun je even vragen of er nog brood is?
dutchnova1-0102.english: Could you quickly ask whether there's any bread left?
dutchnova1-0102.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Could you quickly ask whether there's any bread left?
dutchnova1-0102.explanation: Of introduces an indirect whether-question; is goes to the end and nog marks remaining stock. The base sentence is Kun je even kijken of er nog bloem is?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Kun je even kijken of er nog bloem is?
example.english: Ask a shop assistant to check whether something is available.

dutchnova1-0103.text: Ik gebruik zelfrijzende bloem om pannenkoeken te maken.
dutchnova1-0103.english: I use self-raising flour to make pancakes.
dutchnova1-0103.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I use self-raising flour to make pancakes.
dutchnova1-0103.explanation: Om ... te maken states purpose; this changes the product use while retaining the Belgian flour term. The base sentence is Ik zoek zelfrijzende bloem om een cake te bakken.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik zoek zelfrijzende bloem om een cake te bakken.
example.english: Tell a shop assistant you're looking for self-raising flour for a cake.

dutchnova1-0104.text: Ik heb koffie gekocht omdat die goedkoper was.
dutchnova1-0104.english: I bought coffee because it was cheaper.
dutchnova1-0104.scenario: In a market situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I bought coffee because it was cheaper.
dutchnova1-0104.explanation: Omdat introduces the reason with was at the end, and die can refer to the de-word koffie. The base sentence is Ik heb rijst gekocht omdat die in promotie was.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb rijst gekocht omdat die in promotie was.
example.english: Tell a friend you bought the rice because it was on promotion.

dutchnova1-0105.text: Mag ik nog een beetje soep?
dutchnova1-0105.english: May I have a little more soup?
dutchnova1-0105.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: May I have a little more soup?
dutchnova1-0105.explanation: Nog een beetje is a natural additional small mass-food portion, rather than nog een soep unless a bowl is meant. The base sentence is Mag ik nog wat rijst?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Mag ik nog wat rijst?
example.english: At dinner, ask whether you can have another helping of rice.

dutchnova1-0106.text: Ik eet 's avonds graag samen met vrienden.
dutchnova1-0106.english: I enjoy eating with friends in the evenings.
dutchnova1-0106.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I enjoy eating with friends in the evenings.
dutchnova1-0106.explanation: Graag expresses enjoying the action and 's avonds marks a repeated evening habit. The base sentence is Ik drink 's morgens graag koffie.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik drink 's morgens graag koffie.
example.english: Tell a colleague you like drinking coffee in the morning.

dutchnova1-0107.text: Vind je deze taart ook lekker?
dutchnova1-0107.english: Do you think this cake tastes good too?
dutchnova1-0107.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: Do you think this cake tastes good too?
dutchnova1-0107.explanation: Vinden ... lekker concerns taste; deze agrees with de taart and ook adds another opinion. The base sentence is Ik vind deze soep erg lekker.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik vind deze soep erg lekker.
example.english: Tell your friend you like the taste of the soup.

dutchnova1-0108.text: Ik lust geen olijven, maar wel paprika.
dutchnova1-0108.english: I don't like olives, but I do like peppers.
dutchnova1-0108.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I don't like olives, but I do like peppers.
dutchnova1-0108.explanation: Geen negates food preference and wel makes the positive contrast with a second food. The base sentence is Ik lust geen champignons, maar wel uien.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik lust geen champignons, maar wel uien.
example.english: Tell the host you do not like mushrooms but you do like onions.

dutchnova1-0109.text: Ik heb nog niet geluncht, maar ik heb al thee gedronken.
dutchnova1-0109.english: I haven't had lunch yet, but I've already had tea.
dutchnova1-0109.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I haven't had lunch yet, but I've already had tea.
dutchnova1-0109.explanation: Nog niet and al contrast unfinished lunch with completed drinking in one coordinated sentence. The base sentence is Ik heb nog niet ontbeten, maar ik heb al koffie gedronken.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik heb nog niet ontbeten, maar ik heb al koffie gedronken.
example.english: Say you haven't had breakfast yet, but you've already had coffee.

dutchnova1-0110.text: Mag ik een koud drankje en een verse koek?
dutchnova1-0110.english: May I have a cold drink and a fresh biscuit?
dutchnova1-0110.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: May I have a cold drink and a fresh biscuit?
dutchnova1-0110.explanation: Koud has no -e with indefinite singular het drankje; verse takes -e with de koek. The base sentence is Mag ik een vers broodje en een warme drank?; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Mag ik een vers broodje en een warme drank?
example.english: Ask for a fresh sandwich and a warm drink.

dutchnova1-0111.text: Ik wil graag een klein stukje chocolade.
dutchnova1-0111.english: I'd like a small piece of chocolate.
dutchnova1-0111.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: I'd like a small piece of chocolate.
dutchnova1-0111.explanation: Klein is uninflected before indefinite singular het stukje; graag makes the request polite. The base sentence is Ik wil alleen een klein stukje taart.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: Ik wil alleen een klein stukje taart.
example.english: Explain that you want only a small piece of cake.

dutchnova1-0112.text: We hebben nog maar twee eieren in huis.
dutchnova1-0112.english: We only have two eggs left at home.
dutchnova1-0112.scenario: In a food situation, communicate this new situation in Dutch: We only have two eggs left at home.
dutchnova1-0112.explanation: Nog maar emphasizes scarcity, and in huis gives the location of the remaining stock. The base sentence is We hebben nog maar een beetje melk.; notice how the changed setting or construction affects the meaning.

example.text: We hebben nog maar een beetje melk.
example.english: You are nearly out of milk; tell your housemate there's only a little left.
